title: Two Sum II Input Array Is Sorted
description:
An array numbers is sorted in nondecreasing order. Find two different positions whose values add to target, and return their 1-based indices in increasing order. Exactly one pair of positions works.

Sorting gives you more than a faster search: if the sum of the values at the two ends is too small, moving the left end inward is the only move that can increase it; if it is too large, move the right end instead. Find the pair without using extra space proportional to the array length.

Example 1:

Input: numbers = [2,7,11,15], target = 9
Output: [1,2]

Example 2:

Input: numbers = [-5,-1,0,6], target = 1
Output: [1,4]

Example 3:

Input: numbers = [3,3], target = 6
Output: [1,2]

Constraints:

  • 2 <= numbers.length <= 30,000
  • -1,000 <= numbers[i], target <= 1,000
  • numbers is sorted in nondecreasing order; exactly one pair of distinct indices has the required sum.
  • Use O(1) auxiliary space.

exampleTestCases.explanation: The first two values sum to 9; positions start at 1.
Both positions hold 3, and they are distinct indices.
